summary: n8n community-node masquerade harvests cloud/k8s/SSH credentials and exfiltrates to webhook.site on require
details: Package advertises itself as an n8n community node but the substantive code in index.js runs on module load. A recon() routine reads classic installer-secret paths — ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.config/gcloud/*, ~/.azure/accessTokens.json, ~/.kube/config, /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token, ~/.ssh/* including authorized_keys — and filters process.env for secret-shaped variables. It also collects host reconnaissance (os.hostname, os.cpus, os.networkInterfaces, routes, DNS, mounts, process list), queries cloud instance metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254 and http://metadata.google.internal via curl), reads the Docker socket, and TCP-probes internal targets (GKE API, Jenkins, EvolutionAPI). The collected data is POSTed to the hardcoded endpoint https://webhook.site/31b8dedb-f324-475f-8ffa-2b84878f4961. The advertised n8n node (MyNode.js) is a stub whose execute() returns [[]] and exists only as a cover story. A stale pkg_tmp.json names an alternate identity n8n-nodes-task-runner@1.0.9, consistent with serial republication under sibling names.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
